newsitem.title: INDIA: Finolex launches fibre optic cable plant.
newsitem.headline: Finolex launches fibre optic cable plant.

text.p: India's Finolex Cables Ltd and Lucent Technologies of the U.S. have launched a joint venture plant to manufacture fibre optic cables at Pune near Bombay, the company said on Monday.

The joint venture, AT&T Finolex Fibre Optic Cables, will operate and manage the state-of-the-art plant which has an annual production capacity of 10,000 km of cable. It began operations on January 1, the company said.
"We are pleased to see the successful take-off of the plant," P.P. Chabria, chairman of the Finolex group, said in a statement.
"Our combined strengths in the joint venture will bring the latest in fibre optic technology quickly to meet India's pressing communications needs now and in the 21st century."

Finolex Cables Ltd, which has a turnover of 5.1 billion rupees, is part of India's diversified Finolex Group. Lucent Technologies, the former systems and telecommunications arm of AT&T, is a world leader in fibre optic technology, and was the first to invent the multimode fibre in 1981.
The statement said AT&T Finolex intends to manufacture, market and sell international grade die-electric and armoured fibre optic cables to the $70-million Indian telecommunication market.

AT&T Finolex's target customers include the department of telecommunications, private basic service operators and private cellular operators, public sector oil companies and electricity boards, it said.
